request.purpose: Compute the conditional lever-rule map from assumed total variant RNA mass fraction to dilute-phase volume fraction for each supplied E04 tie-line; quantify how the result changes across endpoint marginal-error corners and compare the relative partition ratios. This tests a conditional mechanism consequence, not whether B follows it.

variables_units.x_var: variant fraction by total RNA mass, dimensionless assumed 0..1

assumptions: Closed two-phase system, conserved reference and variant masses, fixed coexisting endpoints within each tie-line, and no third component or source/sink during the algebraic lever-rule calculation.
x_var is a hypothetical independently measured RNA mass fraction; DNA read fractions are not RNA fractions.
Supplied marginal lower/upper endpoint bounds are varied as corners for sensitivity only; do not call them confidence intervals.
E04 endpoints are not B time-course measurements and do not identify an internal cavity phase or image geometry.
model_spec.range_conditions: For each tie_line_id 0,1,2, evaluate x_var=0,0.1,...,1.0. Compute phi_l=(C_var,d-r*C_ref,d)/(r*(C_ref,l-C_ref,d)-(C_var,l-C_var,d)), r=x_var/(1-x_var); handle x_var=1 with the species-only limit. Retain only values in [0,1] as lever-rule-compatible; flag invalid values. Recompute at all combinations of lower/upper supplied endpoint bounds (16 corners per tie-line), skipping undefined K ratios when a dilute concentration is zero. Include central endpoint K_ref,K_var and K_var/K_ref where defined. Report residual reconstruction of normalized masses for valid points, equal-partition/zero-species/degenerate checks, and whether relative preference direction differs across tie-lines.

request.missing_relation: Whether multicomponent RNA condensates or coacervates can form compositionally distinct coexisting phases with preferential partitioning that is physically capable of creating an internal RNA-poor compartment, and what thermodynamic or wetting conditions are required.
request.conditions: Background first published on or before 2025-05-12; exclude target identity and post-cutoff accounts. Search general RNA coacervate/condensate compartmentalization and multiphase organization, not the specific case.
request.query: RNA coacervate condensate multiphase compartmentalization internal compartments preferential partitioning wetting RNA species
request.change_if_found: If qualified literature directly supports internal compartment formation by compositionally distinct RNA-rich/RNA-poor coexisting phases under stated conditions, add that relation as bounded background support and retain the required untested mapping to this case. If only general phase coexistence or protein-only examples are found, do not use them as evidence that this RNA case forms cavities; retain H1 strictly as a hypothesis or revise toward an alternative mechanism.

request.purpose: Test the algebraic lever rule under equal partition selectivity, identical concentrations across phases, a degenerate 0/0 case and an incompatible composition; report whether phase fraction is identifiable and check mass balance where it is.

variables_units.M_ref,M_var: ng for arbitrary total volume 1 uL

assumptions: Synthetic values are algebraic unit tests, not empirical values for E04 or B.
Closed two-phase system, conserved masses, fixed endpoint concentrations, total volume 1 uL.
Equal selectivity means K_var=C_var,d/C_var,l equals K_ref=C_ref,d/C_ref,l while each species may differ across phases.
model_spec.range_conditions: Case A: ref d/l=10/1 and var d/l=20/2 (both K=10); test r=2 and r=1. Case B: identical endpoint concentration within each species across phases (ref 10/10, var 2/2); test r=0.2. Case C: equal-K case with r=2 where numerator and denominator vanish, plus a chosen r yielding nonzero numerator and zero denominator. Return analytic status and, for any identified phi, reconstruct both masses; do not infer empirical support.

request.missing_relation: Direct experimental evidence, if available before cutoff, that RNA-containing condensates form internal compositionally distinct compartments, and conditions such as coexisting phase composition, wetting or interfacial tensions that determine internal versus external organization.
request.conditions: First published on or before 2025-05-12; general background only, exclude target identity and post-cutoff descriptions. Prior S1 returned only two review abstracts, neither directly establishing internal RNA-poor compartments.
request.query: RNA condensate internal compartment multiphase RNA coacervate wetting interfacial tension experimental
request.change_if_found: Use direct experimental relation only within its measured species and conditions; if results concern general phase separation or protein-only compartments, retain them as limited analogy and leave internal RNA-poor cavity formation as an unverified hypothesis.
